judge.note: rule-based provision judge; no model call, no judge cost

pricing.rate_basis: peak (the higher of the provider's published rates)

cost_estimate.basis: upper bound: the measured prompt length for every request and max_tokens for every completion

on_zero_correct_in_L7.wording: report the zero, do not describe it as a comparator artefact

on_all_correct_in_L7.wording: report the absence of the incorrect class

on_both_classes_in_L7.action: report the counts, the uncertainty and the interval; a sparse class must be stated explicitly and no gate is claimed

on_sparse_class.action: flag as sparse and refuse to present the AUROC as a ranking

outcome_rules.slices: L1 and L7 reported separately; pooled AUROC never presented as detector or method performance

prompt_token_estimate.method: ceil(len(system_prompt + question) / 4), max taken for the ceiling

privacy.what_is_sent: the system prompt and one synthetic legal question per request, plus the model's own replies
what_is_not_sent: no client data, no case files, no personal data
no frozen run artefacts, no scores, no labels
no repository contents other than the prompt text
privacy.data_origin: synthetic items generated from the published IPC/BNS successor mapping; the slice is flagged verified=false
privacy.provider_retention: governed by the chosen provider's API terms; DeepSeek and OpenAI both retain request data for abuse monitoring under their standard terms unless a zero-retention arrangement is in place
privacy.residual_risk: the questions themselves are not confidential, but they would leave the machine; the legal caveat is that the dataset is unverified, so the answers are not legal advice and must not be published as such
